answer: A Weekly community check-in streak over six months verified by signed timestamps makes identity a record of showing up: every week the applicant signs in, the signed timestamps go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so the network trusts the account that was there every week, not the one that appeared yesterday. Without this check, a gale of fresh fake accounts could appear overnight. From the thread to the ledge, the same rule holds: no presence, no trust, no exception.
